title: Research, Innovation & Development
text:
Fabio A. Cruz Sanchez
Mauricio Camargo
Ferney Osorio

This introduction course seeks to to Master and Engineering students to the basis of the scientific research in Innovation Management field. The main purpose is to understand the process of establishing a research process pipeline, including the literature review, structuration of the research problematic, definition of experimental protocol and hypothesis and presentation of the results in from of a scientific paper. Moreover, an overview of the
avoir une première vue d’ensemble sur l’organisation et les modes de financement de la recherche.
This course includes a course in presences and a writing workshop of a first scientific paper.

::: {.column width="50%"} ::: aside Source: Rojon, C. & Saunders, M. N. K. Formulating a convincing rationale for a research study. Coaching: An International Journal of Theory, Research and Practice 5, 55–61 (2012). ::: ::: ::::

title: What is Scientific Research?
text:
Good research question: Descriptive + Explanatory
Being able to provide meaningful explanations requires answers to ‘why’ (i.e. explanatory) questions in addition to ‘what’ (i.e. descriptive) questions.
For example:

'How effective is the coaching process at helping coachees to solve a problem they experience and what are the reasons for this?'
'To what extent is the coaching process effective at helping coachees solve a problem and why?'

::: aside Source: Rojon, C. & Saunders, M. N. K. Formulating a convincing rationale for a research study. Coaching: An International Journal of Theory, Research and Practice 5, 55–61 (2012). :::
